［#54］
Pruning parameters For all models, an iterative pruning rate of 0.2 was used and 30 pruning iterations were performed. Following the sixth pruning iteration, model performance was evaluated every third pruning iteration. Pruning was performed using magnitude pruning, such that the smallest magnitude weights were removed first, as in [12, 19]. For Fashion-MNIST, SVHN, CIFAR-10 and CIFAR-100 winning tickets, late resetting of 1 epoch was used. For ImageNet and Places365 winning tickets, late resetting of 3 epochs was used.

［#56］
Figure A1: Comparison of different random masks. Performance of various random masks on CIFAR-10. Error bars represent mean ± standard deviation across six random seeds.

［#57］
When models are pruned in an unstructured manner, there are two aspects of the final pruned model that may be informative: the values of the weights themselves and the structure of the mask used for pruning. In the original lottery ticket study [7], bad tickets were compared with randomly drawn values, but the preserved winning ticket mask. related_claims.content: Comparing (a) preserved winning-ticket masks, (b) masks permuted only within layers (local permutation), and (c) masks permuted across all layers (global permutation) shows that locally permuting a mask degrades performance moderately while globally permuting the mask degrades performance dramatically.

For obtaining competitive winning tickets in the large-model and large-dataset regime of natural-image classification, an iterative magnitude-pruning schedule with pruning fraction per iteration 0.2 (20% of remaining parameters) over up to 30 iterations combined with late resetting to parameters at a small early training iteration—resetting to the parameters after 1 epoch for Fashion-MNIST, SVHN, CIFAR-10 and CIFAR-100, and after 3 epochs for ImageNet and Places365—produced effective winning tickets, with learning-rate annealing schedules and other hyperparameters matched per model family.

Winning-ticket initializations discovered by iterative magnitude pruning on ImageNet, Places365, and, to a lesser extent, CIFAR-100 produce sparse initializations that, when used to train a VGG19 or ResNet50 architecture on SVHN, Fashion-MNIST, CIFAR-10, CIFAR-100, ImageNet, and Places365, frequently achieve test accuracies on the target tasks that are close to the accuracies obtained by winning tickets discovered directly on those target datasets.
